summary: Integer division by zero (SIGFPE) in divideInterval() when a rank has no local atoms (list->inum == 0).
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:254-256: 'nAtomBlocks = calculateNumberOfIntervals(inum, atomBlockSize); if (nAtomBlocks > 100) nAtomBlocks = 100; divideInterval(atomBlocks, inum, nAtomBlocks);'.  calculateNumberOfIntervals (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:475-483) returns 'M = N/intervalSize' = 0 for N==0 and does not bump it because 'N % intervalSize != 0' is false.  divideInterval (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:461-472) then executes 'int intervalSize = N / M;' and 'int remainder = N % M;' with M==0.  The CPU base never reaches this code: PairPOD::compute() uses the blockMode==0 branch (src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:187-233) and the block code (pair_pod.cpp:236-239) is dead.
failure_scenario: Any MPI rank whose subdomain momentarily contains no local atoms (dilute system, strong load imbalance, or simply more ranks than atoms) -> list->inum == 0 -> integer division by zero -> SIGFPE / undefined behavior at the first force evaluation.
suggested_fix: Return early from compute() when inum == 0 (after ev_init and the per-atom array setup), or clamp nAtomBlocks to at least 1 in calculateNumberOfIntervals().

summary: Only the two-body slice of the base-descriptor array bd is zeroed; the d3/d4/d33/d34/d44 slices are left stale when their Nij guards fail (the zeroing calls are commented out), whereas the CPU code zeroes all Ni*Mdesc entries.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:1415 'set_array_to_zero(d2, Ni*nl2);' is the only zeroing; :1436 '//set_array_to_zero(d3, Ni*nl3);' and :1445 '//set_array_to_zero(d4, Ni*nl4);' are commented out and there is no zeroing at all for d33/d34/d44.  The CPU counterpart starts with a full wipe: src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:1797 'for (int i=0; i<Ni*Mdesc; i++) bd1[i] = 0.0;' and EAPOD::peratomenergyforce2 does the same (src/ML-POD/eapod.cpp:1207 'for (int i=0; i<Mdesc; i++) bd[i] = 0.0;').
failure_scenario: A block whose total pair count drops to Nij<=1 (e.g. a 2-atom dimer stretched beyond rcut after a step where it was bonded): d3/d4/d33/d34/d44 keep the values written on the previous step/block and are multiplied by the POD coefficients in blockatom_base_coefficients -> wrong energy and forces, silently.
suggested_fix: Restore an unconditional 'set_array_to_zero(bd, Ni*Mdesc)' at the top of blockatom_base_descriptors().

summary: 'neighflag' is read in compute() but never initialized on host execution, because init_style() returns early before assigning it.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.h:50 declares 'int neighflag;' and the constructor (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:47-67) never initializes it.  init_style() (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:89-96) does 'if (host_flag) { ...; PairPOD::init_style(); return; }' and only the non-host path reaches ':101 neighflag = lmp->kokkos->neighflag;'.  compute() then reads it at :192 'if (neighflag == FULL) no_virial_fdotr_compute = 1;'.  host_flag is 1 for every CPU-only KOKKOS build (:66 'host_flag = (execution_space == HostKK);' with LMPDeviceType == LMPHostType) and for the pod/kk/host variant.  Contrast pair_pace_kokkos.cpp:774 where neighflag is assigned before any early return that can skip it.
failure_scenario: Serial/OpenMP KOKKOS build running 'pair_style pod/kk': the uninitialized int happens to hold 1 (FULL == 1, kokkos_type.h:27) -> no_virial_fdotr_compute is silently switched on mid-run, changing which virial path Pair::ev_setup selects; otherwise plain undefined behaviour flagged by sanitizers.
suggested_fix: Initialize neighflag in the constructor (e.g. 'neighflag = lmp->kokkos->neighflag;' or HALF) and/or set it before the host_flag early return in init_style().

summary: The three-/four-body descriptor guards use the per-BLOCK pair count Nij instead of the per-ATOM neighbor count used by the reference EAPOD implementation, so atoms with 0/1/2 neighbours get non-zero 3-/4-body descriptors in pod/kk but zero in pair_style pod.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:1421 'if ((nl3 > 0) && (Nij>1))', :1443 'if ((nl4 > 0) && (Nij>2))', :1452/:1460/:1468 'Nij>3/4/5' - here Nij is the TOTAL number of (i,j) pairs of the whole atom block (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:274 'nij = NeighborCount(numij, rcutsq, gi1, ni);' over up to atomBlockSize=2048 atoms).  The reference used by pair_style pod is EAPOD::peratomenergyforce2 (src/ML-POD/eapod.cpp:1248-1284) where the identical guards 'if ((nl3 > 0) && (Nj>1))', 'if ((nl4 > 0) && (Nj>2))', 'Nj>3/4/5' use Nj = number of neighbours of the SINGLE atom i (called from src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:216 with the per-atom nij).
failure_scenario: An atom with exactly one neighbour inside rcut (gas-phase molecule, evaporated atom, dimer scan): pair_style pod leaves its d3 block zero, pod/kk computes d3 = sum pc3*sumU*sumU != 0 -> different energy and force for that atom.
suggested_fix: Evaluate the guards per atom (numij(i+1)-numij(i)) inside the kernels, or at minimum document/verify that the block-level guard reproduces EAPOD; the safest is to zero the descriptor of atoms with fewer neighbours than the guard requires.

summary: Error message in pod/kk names the wrong pair style ('pair pace/kk'), copied from pair_pace_kokkos.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:107-108: 'if (neighflag == FULL) error->all(FLERR,"Must use half neighbor list style with pair pace/kk");' - identical text to pair_pace_kokkos.cpp:780-781 which legitimately refers to pace.
failure_scenario: A user running pod/kk with 'package kokkos neigh full' is told to fix a pace setting.
suggested_fix: Change the message to name pod/kk.

summary: Unconditional Kokkos::fence() plus std::chrono timestamps around every kernel, even though the timing output is never used (timing flag is always 0).
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:63 'timing = 0;' and nothing ever sets it; comptime[] is accumulated at :277, :284, :291, :306, :1403, :1412, :1419, :1426, :1433, :1440, :1449, :1457, :1465, :1473, :1618, :1630, :1653, :1660 but never printed.  Each accumulation is preceded by an unconditional 'Kokkos::fence()' (:275, :282, :289, :304, :1401, :1410, :1417, :1424, :1431, :1438, :1447, :1455, :1463, :1471, :1617, :1628, :1651, :1658), which serialises the device queue ~18 times per atom block.
failure_scenario: Every timestep pays a full device fence per kernel; on a GPU this removes all kernel overlap and adds host-device round trips for no benefit.
suggested_fix: Guard the fences and chrono calls with 'if (timing)' (or delete the instrumentation).

summary: The host_flag branch allocates three fresh Kokkos views (d_numneigh, d_ilist, d_neighbors) on every single timestep instead of reusing them.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:221-229: 'd_numneigh = typename AT::t_int_1d("pair_pod:numneigh",inum); ... d_ilist = typename AT::t_int_1d("pair_pod:ilist",inum); ... MemoryKokkos::realloc_kokkos(d_neighbors,"neighlist:neighbors",inum,maxn);' inside compute().  Because host_flag is 1 for every CPU-only KOKKOS build, this is the default path there.
failure_scenario: Large CPU KOKKOS runs pay an inum*maxneigh allocation, zero-fill and copy of the whole neighbor list every step.
suggested_fix: Only (re)allocate when inum or maxn grows, as the rest of the style does with grow_atoms()/grow_pairs().

summary: Device kernels call the unqualified C library math functions instead of the Kokkos:: overloads required by the KOKKOS coding rules.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:632 'double dij = sqrt(...)', :643 'double y5 = sqrt(y4);', :644 'double y6 = exp(-1.0/y5);', :648/:651 'exp(-1.0)', :659-:672 'exp(-alpha...)', :678 'sqrt(2.0/(l_rmax))', :681/:689/:697 'sin(a*x0)', :684/:692/:700 'cos(...)', :754 'double dij = sqrt(xx + yy + zz);' - all inside KOKKOS_LAMBDA bodies.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4 requires Kokkos::sqrt / Kokkos::exp / Kokkos::sin / Kokkos::cos in device kernels.
failure_scenario: Portability: back ends that do not pull the C math functions into device scope (and future Kokkos versions) fail to compile or silently fall back to double precision.
suggested_fix: Prefix the calls with Kokkos::.

summary: k_scale/d_scale are allocated but never filled or read, and 'using MathSpecial::powint' is unused; k_cutsq is modified on the host but never synced (it is also never read on device).
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:145-146 allocate k_scale/d_scale; grep shows no other use of d_scale in the file.  :120-121 set and modify_host() k_cutsq but there is no matching 'k_cutsq.template sync<DeviceType>()' and d_cutsq is never referenced in a kernel.  :40 'using MathSpecial::powint;' with no call site.
failure_scenario: No functional impact today, but the unsynced k_cutsq is a trap for anyone who later adds a device read of d_cutsq.
suggested_fix: Delete the unused scale views and powint using-declaration; if d_cutsq is kept, add the sync after modify_host().

summary: The Kokkos neighbour screening drops the base class' 'rsq > 1e-20' guard, so a coincident pair produces a division by zero (NaN energies/forces).
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:553 'if (rsq < l_rcutsq) count++;' and :605 'if (rsq >= l_rcutsq) return;' versus src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:388 'if (rsq < rcutsq && rsq > 1e-20) {' (also pair_pod.cpp:416 and :451).  radialbasis then divides by dij (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:633-635 'dr1 = xij1/dij;') and angularbasis divides by dij3 (:760).
failure_scenario: Two atoms at identical coordinates (overlapping insertion, fix deposit failure, zero-temperature start from a bad structure) enter the pair list -> dij == 0 -> NaN propagates into all forces and energies instead of the pair being skipped as in the CPU style.
suggested_fix: Add the '&& rsq > 1e-20' condition to both the NeighborCount and NeighborList screening tests so the two styles select the same pairs.

summary: Fixed-size stack array 'double tm[10]' in the multi-element radialangularsum kernel overflows when the POD model has more than 10 elements.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:849-858: 'double tm[10]; for (int j=0; j<l_nelements; j++) tm[j] = 0; ... tm[tn] += ...; for (int j=0; j<l_nelements; j++) l_sumU(j + kmi) = ...' with no bound on l_nelements.  (The CPU code has the same 'double sum[10]' at src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:995, and nothing in EAPOD limits nelements.)
failure_scenario: A POD potential fitted for 11 or more elements -> out-of-bounds stack writes inside a device kernel -> silent corruption or crash.
suggested_fix: Add an explicit check in coeff()/copy_from_pod_class() that nelements <= 10, or size the scratch from nelements via team scratch memory.

summary: Several KOKKOS styles set copymode = 1 and then call error->all()/error->one() before resetting it to 0, so on an exception-enabled build the style is left with copymode == 1 and its destructors free nothing (memory leak).
failure_scenario: liblammps/Python (LAMMPS_EXCEPTIONS=on): a run that trips e.g. "Bad FENE bond" or "requires 'newton on'" throws out of compute(); the caller catches it and later closes LAMMPS. Every destructor in the style's chain sees copymode == 1 and returns immediately, so eatom/vatom, the style's dual views and Pair/Bond::id/style allocations are all leaked. Repeated catch-and-retry loops (a common Python driver pattern) leak on every failure.
suggested_fix: Hoist the input-validation error->all() checks above the `copymode = 1` line (they do not depend on the kernel), and for genuinely in-kernel failures set copymode = 0 before calling error->one()/error->all().

summary: PairYLZKokkos reads the ellipsoid bonus (quaternion) array on device but leaves BONUS_MASK out of datamask_read, so atomKK->sync() never brings k_bonus to the device and stale quaternions are used.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_ylz_kokkos.cpp:52 `datamask_read = X_MASK | F_MASK | TORQUE_MASK | TYPE_MASK | ELLIPSOID_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK;` (no BONUS_MASK), line 95 `atomKK->sync(execution_space,datamask_read);`, line 106 `bonus = avecKK->k_bonus.view<DeviceType>();` and the kernel dereferences `bonus(ibnum).quat` at lines 228 and 269. src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.cpp:908/921 shows k_bonus is only synced when `mask & BONUS_MASK`. Every other KOKKOS style that reads bonus data includes it: compute_erotate_asphere_kokkos.cpp:35 `datamask_read = ... | ELLIPSOID_MASK | BONUS_MASK;`, fix_langevin_kokkos.cpp:618 `atomKK->sync(execution_space,BONUS_MASK|TORQUE_MASK|ANGMOM_MASK|ELLIPSOID_MASK);`, fix_nve_asphere_kokkos.cpp:64/84.
failure_scenario: GPU build: any host-side update of the bonus array marks it host-modified without a matching device sync -- e.g. AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos::unpack_border_bonus / unpack_comm_bonus (src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.cpp:307/364/440 `atomKK->modified(HostKK,datamask_bonus);`) when comm runs on the host, or a non-KOKKOS asphere integrator. pair ylz/kk then evaluates quat_to_mat() on stale (or never-uploaded) ghost quaternions and returns wrong forces and torques with no error. Invisible on CPU-only builds where host and device share memory.
suggested_fix: Add BONUS_MASK to datamask_read in the PairYLZKokkos constructor (and to datamask_modify only if the style ever wrote bonus data, which it does not).

summary: The KOKKOS ylz kernel silently skips atoms that are not ellipsoids, dropping the CPU style's "All atoms for pair style ylz must be ellipsoids" error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_ylz_kokkos.cpp:219-220 `const int ibnum = d_ellipsoid(i);\n  if (ibnum < 0) return;   // skip non-ellipsoid atoms` and 247-248 `const int jbnum = d_ellipsoid(j);\n    if (jbnum < 0) continue;`. The CPU base counts these (src/ASPHERE/pair_ylz.cpp:124-127 and 150-153 `++flag; continue;`) and aborts after the loop (lines 202-204 `MPI_Allreduce(&flag,&flag_all,...); if (flag_all) error->all(FLERR, "All atoms for pair style ylz must be ellipsoids");`).
failure_scenario: A system mixing point particles and ellipsoids: pair_style ylz errors out and tells the user what is wrong; pair_style ylz/kk silently omits every interaction involving a point particle and reports plausible-looking but wrong energies and forces.
suggested_fix: Set a device flag when a non-ellipsoid atom is skipped, MPI_Allreduce it after the kernel and raise the same error message.

summary: datamask_read carries ELLIPSOID_MASK but not BONUS_MASK, although the kernel dereferences bonus(ibnum).quat and bonus(jbnum).quat. atomKK->sync() therefore never brings the ellipsoid bonus array to the device, so stale or never-uploaded quaternions are used.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pair_ylz_kokkos.cpp:52 vs the reads at :228 and :269; grep BONUS_MASK over the file returns nothing. AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos syncs k_bonus only under 'mask & BONUS_MASK'. Styles that get it right: compute_erotate_asphere_kokkos.cpp:35, fix_nve_asphere_kokkos.cpp:64.)

summary: cutsq_custom is declared as int instead of double, so the trim cutoff squared is truncated to an integer and neighbors are dropped (or all of them dropped when the cutoff is below 1.0).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.h:283 'int nlocal,num_skip,cutsq_custom;'.  It is filled with a floating point value in src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:50 'cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom;' and compared against a double in :144 'if (rsq > cutsq_custom) continue;'.  Every other npair trim class stores it as double: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.h:248 'double cutsq_custom;', src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.h:366 'double cutsq_custom,delta;', src/npair_skip.cpp:68 'double cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom * cutoff_custom;'.
failure_scenario: skip/trim/kk/* list with cutoff_custom = 3.5 -> cutsq_custom = int(12.25) = 12, so neighbor pairs at 3.465 < r <= 3.5 A are silently dropped from the list; with cutoff_custom < 1.0 (e.g. a short-range fix list) cutsq_custom becomes 0 and the list is emptied entirely, zeroing all forces from that sub-style.
suggested_fix: Change the declaration to 'int nlocal,num_skip; double cutsq_custom;'.

summary: cutsq_custom is declared as int in the skip functor ('int nlocal,num_skip,cutsq_custom;') although it is assigned cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom and compared against a double rsq, so the trim cutoff is truncated and neighbours are dropped (all of them when the cutoff is below 1.0).
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.h:106 vs the assignment at npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:50 and the test at :144; the sibling functors declare it double - npair_trim_kokkos.h:51 and npair_halffull_kokkos.h:366).

summary: For wallstyle ZCYLINDER with the 'shear' keyword the wall velocity vwall is accumulated with += inside the per-atom loop, so every contacting atom sees a wall velocity contaminated by all previously processed atoms.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:602-608 sets vwall once before the loop ('vwall[0] = vwall[1] = vwall[2] = 0.0; ... else if (wshear) vwall[axis] = vshear;'), then inside the 'for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; i++)' loop at lines 666-670: 'if (wshear && axis != 2) { vwall[0] += vshear * x[i][1]/delxy; vwall[1] += -vshear * x[i][0]/delxy; vwall[2] = 0.0; }'. vwall is never reset per atom, so the rotational wall velocity of atom i is added on top of the values left by atoms 0..i-1 (and on top of the pre-loop vwall[axis]=vshear).
failure_scenario: fix f all wall/gran/old hooke ... zcylinder 10.0 shear x 1.0 : with N atoms in contact with the cylinder, the effective wall velocity used for atom k is sum over all previous contacting atoms, growing without bound -> wrong tangential/damping forces and unphysical heating.
suggested_fix: Compute the rotational wall velocity into a per-atom local copy (e.g. 'double vwall_local[3] = {0,0,0}; vwall_local[0] = vshear*x[i][1]/delxy; ...') and pass that to the interaction routines instead of mutating the shared vwall array.

summary: init() increments roll_history_index / twist_history_index before they are ever assigned when the corresponding history is disabled, reading uninitialized members.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:519-541: roll_history_index is only assigned inside 'if (roll_history) {...}' and twist_history_index only inside 'if (twist_history) {...}', but lines 533-537 do 'if (normal_model == JKR) { tangential_history_index += 1; roll_history_index += 1; twist_history_index += 1; }' and lines 538-541 do the same for MINDLIN_RESCALE unconditionally. Neither index is initialized in the constructor (header src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.h:80-82 declares them plain ints).
failure_scenario: fix wall/gran/old granular jkr ... tangential linear_history ... (no rolling/twisting): roll_history_index and twist_history_index are read while indeterminate; harmless today only because granular() guards their use with roll_model/twist_model, but it is undefined behaviour and trips MemorySanitizer/valgrind.
suggested_fix: Initialize normal_history_index/tangential_history_index/roll_history_index/twist_history_index to 0 in the constructor (or at the top of init()) before the conditional increments.

summary: roll_model and twist_model are left uninitialized when pairstyle is not GRANULAR.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:87-90 initializes 'normal_model = NORMAL_NONE; tangential_model = TANGENTIAL_NONE; damping_model = DAMPING_NONE;' but roll_model/twist_model are assigned only in the GRANULAR branch at line 127 ('roll_model = twist_model = NONE;'). For pairstyle HOOKE/HOOKE_HISTORY/HERTZ_HISTORY they stay indeterminate; the header src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.h:70 declares them without initializer.
failure_scenario: Any derived/accelerated variant or future code that queries roll_model/twist_model outside the GRANULAR branch (e.g. FixWallGranKokkos) reads garbage; with the CPU code path it is currently latent only because granular() is not called.
suggested_fix: Set 'roll_model = ROLL_NONE; twist_model = TWIST_NONE;' next to the other model defaults at line 88 so they are always defined.

summary: array_atom allocated by grow_arrays() when the 'contacts' keyword is used is never freed in the destructor.
evidence: grow_arrays (src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:1567-1572) does 'if (peratom_flag) memory->grow(array_atom,nmax,size_peratom_cols,"fix_wall_gran_old:array_atom");' but the destructor (lines 476-491) only frees idregion, history_one and mass_rigid.
failure_scenario: 'fix ... wall/gran/old ... contacts' followed by 'unfix' (or repeated fix/unfix in a loop) leaks nmax*8 doubles per instance.
suggested_fix: Add 'memory->destroy(array_atom);' to ~FixWallGranOld() (after the copymode guard).

summary: The kernel that fills elems iterates over atom->nmax instead of nlocal+nghost, so it reads uninitialized entries of atom->type and uses them to index the element map view, which is only ntypes+1 long.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:186-189 'Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType>(0,nmax), KOKKOS_LAMBDA (int i) { const int itype = type(i); d_elems(i) = map(itype); });' -- the CPU original loops only over the valid atoms, src/ML-IAP/mliap_data.cpp:206-209 'for (int i = 0; i < nall; i++) { const int itype = type[i]; elems[i] = map[itype]; }' with 'int nall = atom->nlocal + atom->nghost;' (line 118). nmax is atom->nmax (set at src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:72-73), so indices in [nall, nmax) hold whatever was last in the type array, or uninitialized memory right after Atom::grow(). The map view is allocated with exactly ntypes+1 entries: src/KOKKOS/pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp:159 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_map, map, n+1, "pair_mliap:map");'.
failure_scenario: pair_style mliap/kk immediately after the atom arrays are grown (e.g. the first steps of a run, or after a large migration): type(i) for i >= nlocal+nghost is an arbitrary int, so map(itype) reads outside the ntypes+1 map allocation. With Kokkos bounds checking enabled the run aborts; without it, it is a silent out-of-bounds read (and a segfault if the index is far enough out).
suggested_fix: Launch the kernel over RangePolicy(0, nall) (nlocal+nghost) as the CPU version does, matching the deep_copy that already zeroes the rest of d_elems.

summary: grow_neigharrays() declares an unused host mirror of cutsq, producing an unused-variable warning.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:225-227 'auto d_cutsq=k_pairmliap->k_cutsq.template view<DeviceType>(); auto h_cutsq=k_pairmliap->k_cutsq.view_host(); auto d_numneighs = ...' -- h_cutsq is never referenced again in the function; only d_cutsq is used inside the parallel_reduce at line 244.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; -Wunused-variable noise and a hint that a host/device cutsq mix-up was intended here.
suggested_fix: Delete the h_cutsq line.

summary: k_eatom/k_vatom are destroyed and re-created on every timestep when per-atom energy/virial is requested, instead of the size-guarded reallocation used by the other bond kokkos styles.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_class2_kokkos.cpp:74-87 'if (eflag_atom) { //if(k_eatom.extent(0)<maxeatom) { ... memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"improper:eatom"); ... //} }' - the guard is commented out. The same unconditional destroy/create appears in src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_kokkos.cpp:80-89, src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_expand_kokkos.cpp:76-85 and src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_nm_kokkos.cpp:73-82. The corrected pattern is src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:74-87 'if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { ... } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);'.
failure_scenario: 'compute pe/atom' or 'compute stress/atom' with bond class2/kk or fene/kk on a GPU: a device allocation + free per timestep, which serializes with the kernel stream and can dominate the bond time for small systems.
suggested_fix: Restore the 'if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) {...} else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);' guard in class2, fene, fene/expand and fene/nm, as bond_harmonic_kokkos.cpp already does.

summary: ebond is left uninitialized when eflag == 0 and is then passed by reference into ev_tally(); the CPU base initializes it to 0.0 before the loop.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_class2_kokkos.cpp:180 'KK_FLOAT ebond, fbond, de_bond;' then :186 'if (eflag) ebond = ...;' and :202 'if (EVFLAG) ev_tally(ev,i1,i2,ebond,fbond,delx,dely,delz);'. CPU src/CLASS2/bond_class2.cpp:63 'ebond = 0.0;' before the bond loop. Every other kokkos bond style in this group initializes it (e.g. bond_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:178 'KK_FLOAT ebond = 0;').
failure_scenario: A step with vflag set but eflag clear (e.g. 'compute pressure' without thermo energy) runs the EVFLAG=1 kernel with an indeterminate ebond. ev_tally only reads it under eflag_either, so today it is harmless, but any future eflag_atom/eflag_global refactor turns it into garbage energies, and it trips -Wmaybe-uninitialized / static analysis.
suggested_fix: Initialize as 'KK_FLOAT ebond = 0.0; KK_FLOAT fbond = 0.0;' at line 180, matching the other bond kokkos styles.

summary: PairBondValKokkos::settings() replaces the base class argument check with `narg > 3` and then hard-codes `PairBondVal::settings(2,arg)`, so too-few arguments are never rejected and arg[1] is read out of bounds, while a bogus 3rd argument is silently ignored.
failure_scenario: `pair_style bondval/kk 6.0` (narg==1) passes narg=2 to the base, which dereferences arg[1] -- a stale/dangling pointer left in Input::arg from a previous command -> garbage cut_global or a segfault. `pair_style bondval/kk 6.0 4.0 junk` (narg==3) is accepted and `junk` silently ignored, whereas the CPU style errors out.
suggested_fix: Check `if (narg != 2) utils::missing_cmd_args(FLERR, "pair_style bondval", error);` (or simply forward narg unchanged: `PairBondVal::settings(narg,arg);`).

summary: In single/mixed precision builds the two Boltzmann factors of angle mwlc/kk can both underflow float to zero, making Q = 0 and turning the force and energy into NaN.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_mwlc_kokkos.cpp:170-180: 'const KK_FLOAT kbt = d_temp[type] * boltz; ... const KK_FLOAT q = Kokkos::exp(-d_k1[type] * (1.0 + c) / kbt); const KK_FLOAT qm = Kokkos::exp((-d_k2[type] * (1.0 + c) - d_mu[type]) / kbt); const KK_FLOAT Q = q + qm; ... if (eflag) eangle = -kbt * Kokkos::log(Q) - v_min; const KK_FLOAT a = (d_k1[type] * q + d_k2[type] * qm) / Q;'. With LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE or LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_DOUBLE, KK_FLOAT is float (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:400-408) and expf underflows to 0 below about -88, whereas the CPU version (src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_mwlc.cpp:115-121) works in double and only underflows below about -745. In metal units kbt = 8.617e-5 * T, so at T = 300 K a bending constant k1 of ~0.4 eV already gives an exponent of -88 at c = 1.
failure_scenario: A mwlc/kk run built with -DLMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_DOUBLE, metal units, temp 300 and k1 = k2 = 0.5 (eV): for nearly straight angles q = qm = 0, a = 0/0 = NaN and eangle = -kbt*log(0) = inf, so the whole trajectory becomes NaN while the double-precision build and the CPU style are fine.
suggested_fix: Factor out the larger exponent (compute emin_exp = min of the two exponents and evaluate Q = exp(e1-emin_exp) + exp(e2-emin_exp) with the log shifted accordingly), or evaluate the Boltzmann factors in KK_ACC_FLOAT.

summary: update_force() allocates a fresh f_merge_copy device view on every force evaluation, although the code further down already grows it on demand.
failure_scenario: dynamical_matrix does 6*N force evaluations; each one performs (and frees) a 3*nmax device allocation, which serialises against the device stream and dominates the runtime for large systems on a GPU.
suggested_fix: Drop the line 152 allocation and rely on the size check at lines 282-285 (same as VerletKokkos does).

summary: The device-side minimum_image() applies at most a single box-length wrap per dimension (if/else if), whereas Domain::minimum_image() loops (while) until the separation is inside the half box, so a drag point more than ~1.5 box lengths from an atom gets a different image than the CPU fix.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_drag_kokkos.cpp:142-154 `if (m_xperiodic) { if (dx > m_xprd_half) dx -= m_xprd; else if (dx < -m_xprd_half) dx += m_xprd; }` (and the triclinic branch 155-180 likewise). src/domain.cpp Domain::minimum_image(const std::string&,int,double&,double&,double&) uses `while (fabs(dx) > xprd_half) { ... }` in every branch and additionally raises 'Atoms have moved too far apart ... for minimum image' when fabs(dx) > MAXIMGCOUNT*xprd. The CPU fix calls exactly that function: src/EXTRA-FIX/fix_drag.cpp:124 `domain->minimum_image(FLERR, dx,dy,dz);`.
failure_scenario: `fix drag` with a target point specified well outside the periodic box (e.g. box 0..100 and `fix drag all drag 350 50 50 1.0 0.1`): the CPU fix wraps dx three times and pulls atoms toward the nearest image of the target, the /kk fix wraps once and applies a drag force of the wrong direction/magnitude, so ftotal and the trajectory differ between the two. For a target inside the box the two agree.
suggested_fix: Replace the single conditional wraps with `while` loops (as in bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp/dihedral_table_kokkos.cpp, which have the same shortcut but where the separation is bounded), or document/enforce that the drag point must lie inside the box.

summary: Dead DualView members k_cut_ljsq and k_cut_coulsq are declared but never allocated, filled, modified or synced anywhere in the style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_charmm_coul_charmm_implicit_kokkos.h:98 'DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d k_cut_ljsq;' and :100 'DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d k_cut_coulsq;'. grep for k_cut_ljsq/k_cut_coulsq over pair_lj_charmm_coul_charmm_implicit_kokkos.{cpp,h} returns only these two declarations. The device views actually used, d_cut_ljsq/d_cut_coulsq, are created directly in allocate() (pair_lj_charmm_coul_charmm_implicit_kokkos.cpp:298-300) and filled by Kokkos::deep_copy in init_style() (:413-415). The sibling style pair_lj_charmm_coul_charmm_kokkos.h has no such members.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; a reader can mistake them for the buffers backing d_cut_ljsq/d_cut_coulsq and add a sync/modify call against the wrong (empty) view.
suggested_fix: Delete the two unused declarations.
